title: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial: Parabolas & X-Axis Intersections
description: Understand the precise geometrical representation of linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomials. Learn why a degree n polynomial has at most n real zeroes and how parabolic curves opening upward or downward correspond to quadratic zeroes.
key_concepts: Zero of a Polynomial Definition: p(k) = 0
Linear Polynomial Straight Line Graph: Exactly 1 zero at (-b/a, 0)
Quadratic Polynomial Parabola: y = ax² + bx + c opening upward (a > 0) or downward (a < 0)
Three Geometric Cases: Two Distinct Zeroes, Two Coincident Zeroes, No Real Zeroes
Cubic Polynomial Graphs: Up to 3 real x-intercepts
subtopics: Definition of algebraic zeroes vs graphical x-intercepts
Parabolic trajectory analysis and vertex coordinates (-b/2a, -D/4a)
Zeroes of cubic polynomials y = x³ and y = x³ - x

worked_examples.problem: Examine the quadratic polynomial p(x) = x² - 3x - 4. Find its algebraic zeroes and verify them graphically.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = x² - 3x - 4
To find: Zeroes of p(x) and graphical interpretation.
Formula: Set p(x) = 0 ⇒ x² - 3x - 4 = 0
Factorisation: Split middle term: -4x + 1x = -3x, (-4)(1) = -4
x² - 4x + x - 4 = 0
x(x - 4) + 1(x - 4) = 0
(x - 4)(x + 1) = 0 ⇒ x = 4 or x = -1.
Graphical Representation: Plot y = x² - 3x - 4.
Table of values: x = -2 ⇒ y = 6; x = -1 ⇒ y = 0; x = 0 ⇒ y = -4; x = 1.5 ⇒ y = -6.25 (Vertex); x = 4 ⇒ y = 0; x = 5 ⇒ y = 6.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Vertex x = -b/(2a) = -(-3)/(2*1) = 3/2 = 1.5
Vertex y = (1.5)² - 3(1.5) - 4 = 2.25 - 4.5 - 4 = -6.25
Roots: x = (-(-3) ± √(9 - 4(1)(-4))) / 2 = (3 ± √25)/2 = (3 ± 5)/2 ⇒ x = 4, -1.
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are x = -1 and x = 4. The parabola intersects the x-axis at (-1, 0) and (4, 0) ].
concept_questions: Why does the x-coordinate of the intersection point represent the zero of the polynomial?
What decides whether the parabola opens upward like a cup or downward like an umbrella?
Can a quadratic polynomial have 3 real zeroes? Why or why not?
If a parabola never touches the x-axis, does the polynomial still have zeroes in the real number system?

worked_examples.problem: Look at the graph of y = x³ - 4x. Determine the number of zeroes of the polynomial and write their exact values.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: y = x³ - 4x
To find: Zeroes from graph and algebra.
Formula: Set y = 0 ⇒ x(x² - 4) = 0
x(x - 2)(x + 2) = 0 ⇒ x = 0, x = 2, x = -2.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Degree = 3 ⇒ At most 3 real zeroes.
Intersections with x-axis occur at (-2, 0), (0, 0), and (2, 0).
Boxed Answer: [ Number of zeroes = 3. The zeroes are x = -2, x = 0, and x = 2 ].
concept_questions: What is the maximum number of times a polynomial of degree n can intersect the x-axis?
Why does the cubic curve pass through the origin (0, 0)?

common_misconceptions: Counting intersections with the y-axis as zeroes: Only intersections with the x-axis give zeroes of p(x)!
Believing every quadratic equation must have 2 distinct real zeroes: A parabola may touch at 1 point or miss the x-axis completely.

title: Relationship Between Zeroes and Coefficients: Quadratic & Cubic Algebraic Identities
description: Master the rigorous algebraic relationships linking polynomial roots (α, β, γ) to standard polynomial coefficients (a, b, c, d). Covers sum of zeroes, product of zeroes, and polynomial reconstruction.
key_concepts: Factor Theorem Link: If α, β are zeroes, (x - α) and (x - β) are factors
Identity: ax² + bx + c = k(x - α)(x - β) = k[x² - (α + β)x + αβ]
Sum of Zeroes Formula: α + β = -b/a
Product of Zeroes Formula: α·β = c/a
Reconstructing Quadratic: p(x) = k[x² - Sx + P] where S = sum, P = product
Cubic Relations: α + β + γ = -b/a, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a, αβγ = -d/a
subtopics: Proof of α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a by equating coefficients
Symmetric expressions in zeroes: α² + β², 1/α + 1/β, α - β

worked_examples.problem: Example 2 (NCERT): Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial x² + 7x + 10, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = x² + 7x + 10
To find: Zeroes of p(x) and verify relations α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a.
Step 1: Factorise p(x) by splitting the middle term.
We need two numbers whose sum is 7 and product is 10: numbers are 2 and 5.
x² + 7x + 10 = x² + 2x + 5x + 10
= x(x + 2) + 5(x + 2) = (x + 2)(x + 5)
Zeroes: p(x) = 0 ⇒ x + 2 = 0 or x + 5 = 0 ⇒ x = -2 or x = -5.
Let α = -2 and β = -5.

Step 2: Identify coefficients from standard form ax² + bx + c:
a = 1, b = 7, c = 10.

Step 3: Verify Sum of Zeroes:
LHS = α + β = (-2) + (-5) = -7
RHS = -b / a = -(7) / 1 = -7
LHS = RHS. Verified!

Step 4: Verify Product of Zeroes:
LHS = α · β = (-2) × (-5) = 10
RHS = c / a = 10 / 1 = 10
LHS = RHS. Verified!
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check: x = -2 ⇒ (-2)² + 7(-2) + 10 = 4 - 14 + 10 = 0 (True)
Check: x = -5 ⇒ (-5)² + 7(-5) + 10 = 25 - 35 + 10 = 0 (True)
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are -2 and -5. Sum = -7 = -b/a, Product = 10 = c/a. Relationship Verified ].
concept_questions: Why do we equate the polynomial to zero to find its zeroes?
If the coefficient of x is positive, why is the sum of zeroes negative?
What is the value of 1/α + 1/β for this polynomial?

worked_examples.problem: Example 3 (NCERT): Find the zeroes of the polynomial x² - 3 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = x² - 3
To find: Zeroes and verify relations with coefficients.
Step 1: Factorise using identity a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b):
x² - 3 = x² - (√3)² = (x - √3)(x + √3)
Zeroes: x - √3 = 0 or x + √3 = 0 ⇒ x = √3 or x = -√3.
Let α = √3, β = -√3.

Step 2: Identify coefficients from ax² + bx + c:
a = 1, b = 0 (since there is no x term), c = -3.

Step 3: Verification:
Sum: α + β = √3 + (-√3) = 0
Formula: -b/a = -0/1 = 0. (LHS = RHS)
Product: α · β = (√3)(-√3) = -3
Formula: c/a = -3/1 = -3. (LHS = RHS)
[ROUGH_WORK]
(√3)² = 3 ⇒ 3 - 3 = 0
(-√3)² = 3 ⇒ 3 - 3 = 0
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are √3 and -√3. Sum = 0 = -b/a, Product = -3 = c/a. Verified ].

worked_examples.problem: Example 4 (NCERT): Find a quadratic polynomial, the sum and product of whose zeroes are -3 and 2, respectively.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Sum of zeroes (S) = α + β = -3, Product of zeroes (P) = α · β = 2.
To find: The quadratic polynomial p(x).
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - (α + β)x + (α · β) ] = k [ x² - Sx + P ]
Substitution: p(x) = k [ x² - (-3)x + 2 ] = k [ x² + 3x + 2 ]
For simplest polynomial, take k = 1:
p(x) = x² + 3x + 2.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check zeroes: x² + 3x + 2 = (x + 1)(x + 2) = 0 ⇒ x = -1, -2
Sum = (-1) + (-2) = -3 (Matches given)
Product = (-1)(-2) = 2 (Matches given)
Boxed Answer: [ Required polynomial is p(x) = x² + 3x + 2 (or any non-zero multiple k(x² + 3x + 2)) ].
concept_questions: Why is there a minus sign in front of the sum in k[x² - Sx + P]?
Can 2x² + 6x + 4 also be a correct answer? Explain why.

          <text x="24" y="48" fill="#64748B" font-size="11" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif">Fundamental algebraic bridges connecting polynomial roots to its standard coefficients</text>
        </g>
        
  
    <g transform="translate(60, 70)">
      <rect width="460" height="230" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#CBD5E1" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/>
      <text x="24" y="32" fill="#0F172A" font-size="14" font-weight="700">Quadratic Polynomial: p(x) = ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0)</text>
      
      <!-- Sum of zeroes -->
      <rect x="24" y="50" width="412" height="42" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#93C5FD" rx="6"/>
      <text x="36" y="76" fill="#1E40AF" font-size="13" font-weight="700">Sum of Zeroes: α + β = -b / a = -(Coefficient of x) / (Coefficient of x²)</text>

      <rect x="24" y="102" width="412" height="42" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#86EFAC" rx="6"/>
      <text x="36" y="128" fill="#166534" font-size="13" font-weight="700">Product of Zeroes: α · β = c / a = (Constant term) / (Coefficient of x²)</text>
      
      <!-- Polynomial Formation -->
      <rect x="24" y="154" width="412" height="52" fill="#FFFBEB" stroke="#FDE68A" rx="6"/>
      <text x="36" y="174" fill="#92400E" font-size="11" font-weight="700">Polynomial Formation Formula:</text>
      <text x="36" y="194" fill="#B45309" font-size="13" font-weight="700">p(x) = k [ x² - (α + β)x + (α · β) ]  where k is any non-zero real constant</text>
    </g>
    
</svg>

title: Exercise 2.1 Complete Solver: Graphical Zero Extraction for 6 Fundamental Graphs
description: Exhaustive step-by-step resolution of all 6 problems from NCERT Exercise 2.1. Learn to inspect polynomial graphs y = p(x) and determine the exact number of real zeroes with crystalline geometric justifications.
key_concepts: Criterion: Number of zeroes = Number of points where y = p(x) intersects or touches the x-axis
Horizontal Line Graph: Parallel to x-axis ⇒ 0 zeroes
Single Crossing Curve: 1 zero
Three Crossing Curve: 3 zeroes
U-Shaped Parabola Cutting Twice: 2 zeroes
Four Crossing Curve: 4 zeroes
Tangency / Touching without Crossing: Counts as 1 point of contact per touch
subtopics: Full resolution of Exercise 2.1 Question 1 (Parts i to vi)
Board exam answer formulation and justification criteria

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.1 Q1 (i): The graph of y = p(x) is a horizontal straight line parallel to the x-axis (above the origin). Find the number of zeroes of p(x).
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Graph is a horizontal line y = c (c ≠ 0) parallel to the x-axis.
To find: Number of zeroes of p(x).
Governing Rule: The number of zeroes of p(x) is equal to the number of points where the graph intersects the x-axis.
Observation: The given line is parallel to the x-axis and does not intersect or touch the x-axis at any point.
Boxed Answer: [ Number of zeroes = 0. Justification: The graph does not intersect the x-axis ].
concept_questions: What polynomial does a horizontal line represent?
If the horizontal line was the x-axis itself (y = 0), how many zeroes would it have?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.1 Q1 (ii): The graph of y = p(x) starts in quadrant 3, crosses the y-axis, and then crosses the x-axis once in quadrant 1. Find the number of zeroes of p(x).
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Curve intersects the y-axis at 1 point and the x-axis at 1 point.
To find: Number of zeroes of p(x).
Observation: The graph intersects the x-axis at exactly one point.
Note: The intersection with the y-axis is irrelevant for zeroes of p(x).
Boxed Answer: [ Number of zeroes = 1. Justification: The graph intersects the x-axis at only one point ].
concept_questions: Does the y-intercept give a zero of p(x)? What does the y-intercept actually represent?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.1 Q1 (iii): The graph of y = p(x) is an S-shaped cubic curve intersecting the x-axis at three points. Find the number of zeroes of p(x).
worked_examples.solution:
Given: S-shaped continuous polynomial curve.
Observation: Counting the points of intersection along the x-axis from left to right:
1. Cuts negative x-axis at 1 point.
2. Cuts near origin / positive x-axis at 2nd point.
3. Cuts further along positive x-axis at 3rd point.
Total intersections with x-axis = 3.
Boxed Answer: [ Number of zeroes = 3. Justification: The graph intersects the x-axis at three distinct points ].
concept_questions: What is the minimum degree of a polynomial that can produce this graph?

worked_examples.solution:
Given: Parabolic curve opening upwards.

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.1 Q1 (v): The graph of y = p(x) is an oscillating wave curve intersecting the x-axis at four distinct points. Find the number of zeroes of p(x).
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Continuous curve oscillating across the x-axis.
Observation: Tracing along the x-axis, the curve cuts the axis at four separate points.
Boxed Answer: [ Number of zeroes = 4. Justification: The graph intersects the x-axis at four distinct points ].
concept_questions: What is the minimum possible degree of this polynomial?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.1 Q1 (vi): The graph of y = p(x) intersects the x-axis at one negative point, touches the x-axis at one point, and touches the x-axis at another point. Find the number of zeroes of p(x).
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Curve intersects at 1 point and touches at 2 points.
Governing Principle: Points where the curve touches the x-axis without crossing are still points where y = 0 (representing real zeroes with even multiplicity).
Counting: 1 intersection + 1 touch + 1 touch = 3 points where y = 0.
Boxed Answer: [ Number of zeroes = 3. Justification: The graph meets (intersects or touches) the x-axis at three points ].
concept_questions: Why does touching the x-axis count as a zero?
What happens algebraically at a point where a curve touches the x-axis?

title: Exercise 2.2 Part 1 Solver: Finding Zeroes & Verifying Coefficient Relationships (All 6 Parts of Q1)
description: Complete, rigorous solution of NCERT Exercise 2.2 Question 1 covering all 6 parts. Master quadratic splitting of the middle term, common factor extraction, difference of squares, and dual verification of sum and product relationships.
key_concepts: Splitting the Middle Term Method: Finding p and q such that p + q = b and pq = ac
Difference of Squares: a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b)
Missing Linear Term (b = 0): Zeroes are symmetric ±√(-c/a)
Missing Constant Term (c = 0): One zero is always 0
Verification Protocol: Formal side-by-side verification of α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q1 (i): Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial x² - 2x - 8, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = x² - 2x - 8
To find: Zeroes and verify relations α + β = -b/a, αβ = c/a.
Step 1: Factorise by splitting the middle term.
Need p, q such that p + q = -2 and pq = -8 ⇒ p = -4, q = 2.
x² - 2x - 8 = x² - 4x + 2x - 8
= x(x - 4) + 2(x - 4) = (x - 4)(x + 2)
Setting p(x) = 0: x - 4 = 0 or x + 2 = 0 ⇒ x = 4, x = -2.
Let α = 4, β = -2.

Step 2: Coefficients from ax² + bx + c:
a = 1, b = -2, c = -8.

Step 3: Verification of Sum of Zeroes:
LHS = α + β = 4 + (-2) = 2
RHS = -b / a = -(-2) / 1 = 2
LHS = RHS. Verified!

Step 4: Verification of Product of Zeroes:
LHS = α · β = 4 × (-2) = -8
RHS = c / a = -8 / 1 = -8
LHS = RHS. Verified!
[ROUGH_WORK]
ac = 1 × (-8) = -8
Factors of -8 that add to -2: (-4, 2)
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are 4 and -2. Sum = 2 = -b/a, Product = -8 = c/a. Verified ].
concept_questions: What is the sign of the product of zeroes if c and a have opposite signs?
How does splitting the middle term relate to the distributive property?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q1 (ii): Find the zeroes of 4s² - 4s + 1, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(s) = 4s² - 4s + 1
Step 1: Recognise (2s)² - 2(2s)(1) + 1² = (2s - 1)²
Alternatively split middle term: ac = 4 × 1 = 4; need sum -4 ⇒ -2, -2.
4s² - 2s - 2s + 1 = 2s(2s - 1) - 1(2s - 1) = (2s - 1)(2s - 1)
Setting p(s) = 0: 2s - 1 = 0 ⇒ s = 1/2, s = 1/2.
Here we have two equal zeroes: α = 1/2, β = 1/2.

Step 2: Coefficients: a = 4, b = -4, c = 1.

Step 3: Verification:
Sum: α + β = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1
-b / a = -(-4) / 4 = 4/4 = 1. (LHS = RHS)
Product: α · β = (1/2) × (1/2) = 1/4
c / a = 1 / 4. (LHS = RHS)
[ROUGH_WORK]
Discriminant D = b² - 4ac = (-4)² - 4(4)(1) = 16 - 16 = 0
D = 0 confirms real and equal roots.
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are 1/2 and 1/2. Sum = 1 = -b/a, Product = 1/4 = c/a. Verified ].
concept_questions: What does D = 0 tell you about the shape and position of the parabola?
Why must we list 1/2 twice when stating the zeroes of this polynomial?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q1 (iii): Find the zeroes of 6x² - 3 - 7x, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = 6x² - 3 - 7x
Step 1: CRITICAL FIRST STEP - Rearrange into standard descending form ax² + bx + c:
p(x) = 6x² - 7x - 3
Here a = 6, b = -7, c = -3.
ac = 6 × (-3) = -18. Need two numbers summing to -7: -9 and 2.
6x² - 9x + 2x - 3 = 3x(2x - 3) + 1(2x - 3) = (2x - 3)(3x + 1)
Setting p(x) = 0:
2x - 3 = 0 ⇒ x = 3/2
3x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = -1/3
Let α = 3/2, β = -1/3.

Step 2: Verification:
Sum: α + β = 3/2 + (-1/3) = (9 - 2)/6 = 7/6
-b / a = -(-7) / 6 = 7/6. (LHS = RHS)
Product: α · β = (3/2) × (-1/3) = -3/6 = -1/2
c / a = -3 / 6 = -1/2. (LHS = RHS)
[ROUGH_WORK]
Warning: If not rearranged, taking b = -3 and c = -7 will produce a fatal calculation error!
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are 3/2 and -1/3. Sum = 7/6 = -b/a, Product = -1/2 = c/a. Verified ].
concept_questions: Why is rearranging the polynomial into standard form non-negotiable?
What common mistake do students make when reading coefficients from an unarranged polynomial?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q1 (iv): Find the zeroes of 4u² + 8u, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(u) = 4u² + 8u
Step 1: Notice constant term c = 0. Factor out common term 4u:
p(u) = 4u(u + 2)
Setting p(u) = 0: 4u = 0 or u + 2 = 0 ⇒ u = 0, u = -2.
Let α = 0, β = -2.

Step 2: Coefficients: a = 4, b = 8, c = 0.

Step 3: Verification:
Sum: α + β = 0 + (-2) = -2
-b / a = -(8) / 4 = -2. (LHS = RHS)
Product: α · β = 0 × (-2) = 0
c / a = 0 / 4 = 0. (LHS = RHS)
[ROUGH_WORK]
Whenever c = 0, zero is always a root since p(0) = 0.
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are 0 and -2. Sum = -2 = -b/a, Product = 0 = c/a. Verified ].
concept_questions: Can you divide both sides by u to solve 4u² + 8u = 0? Why is dividing by a variable dangerous?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q1 (v): Find the zeroes of t² - 15, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(t) = t² - 15
Step 1: Linear term b = 0. Use difference of squares identity:
t² - 15 = t² - (√15)² = (t - √15)(t + √15)
Setting p(t) = 0: t = √15 or t = -√15.
Let α = √15, β = -√15.

Step 2: Coefficients: a = 1, b = 0, c = -15.

Step 3: Verification:
Sum: α + β = √15 + (-√15) = 0
-b / a = -0 / 1 = 0. (LHS = RHS)
Product: α · β = (√15)(-√15) = -15
c / a = -15 / 1 = -15. (LHS = RHS)
[ROUGH_WORK]
t² = 15 ⇒ t = ±√15
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are √15 and -√15. Sum = 0 = -b/a, Product = -15 = c/a. Verified ].
concept_questions: Why are the zeroes symmetric about the origin on the number line?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q1 (vi): Find the zeroes of 3x² - x - 4, and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = 3x² - x - 4
Step 1: ac = 3 × (-4) = -12. Need two numbers whose sum is -1 and product is -12: -4 and 3.
3x² - 4x + 3x - 4 = x(3x - 4) + 1(3x - 4) = (3x - 4)(x + 1)
Setting p(x) = 0: 3x - 4 = 0 or x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = 4/3, x = -1.
Let α = 4/3, β = -1.

Step 2: Coefficients: a = 3, b = -1, c = -4.

Step 3: Verification:
Sum: α + β = 4/3 + (-1) = (4 - 3)/3 = 1/3
-b / a = -(-1) / 3 = 1/3. (LHS = RHS)
Product: α · β = (4/3) × (-1) = -4/3
c / a = -4 / 3. (LHS = RHS)
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check sum: 4/3 - 1 = 1/3
Check product: (4/3)*(-1) = -4/3
Boxed Answer: [ Zeroes are 4/3 and -1. Sum = 1/3 = -b/a, Product = -4/3 = c/a. Verified ].

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Cubes: α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ - 3αβ(α + β)

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q2 (i): Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively: 1/4, -1.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Sum of zeroes (S) = 1/4, Product of zeroes (P) = -1.
To find: The quadratic polynomial.
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - Sx + P ]
Substitution: p(x) = k [ x² - (1/4)x + (-1) ] = k [ x² - x/4 - 1 ]
To obtain integer coefficients, choose k = 4 (the denominator):
p(x) = 4(x² - x/4 - 1) = 4x² - x - 4.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check zeroes of 4x² - x - 4:
Sum = -b/a = -(-1)/4 = 1/4 (Matches)
Product = c/a = -4/4 = -1 (Matches)
Boxed Answer: [ Required quadratic polynomial is 4x² - x - 4 ].
concept_questions: Why does multiplying the polynomial by k not alter its zeroes?
What would happen if we chose k = 1 instead of k = 4?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q2 (ii): Find a quadratic polynomial with sum = √2, product = 1/3.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: S = √2, P = 1/3.
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - Sx + P ] = k [ x² - √2 x + 1/3 ]
Choose k = 3 (LCM of denominators):
p(x) = 3(x² - √2 x + 1/3) = 3x² - 3√2 x + 1.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check: Sum = -(-3√2)/3 = √2
Product = 1/3
Boxed Answer: [ Required quadratic polynomial is 3x² - 3√2 x + 1 ].
concept_questions: Is 3x² - 3√2x + 1 a polynomial with rational coefficients? Why is the middle term irrational?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q2 (iii): Find a quadratic polynomial with sum = 0, product = √5.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: S = 0, P = √5.
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - 0·x + √5 ]
Taking k = 1:
p(x) = x² + √5.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Zeroes: x² = -√5 (No real zeroes, but the polynomial definition is completely valid!)
Sum = 0, Product = √5
Boxed Answer: [ Required quadratic polynomial is x² + √5 ].
concept_questions: Does a polynomial whose product of zeroes is positive always have real zeroes?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q2 (iv): Find a quadratic polynomial with sum = 1, product = 1.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: S = 1, P = 1.
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - Sx + P ] = k [ x² - 1·x + 1 ]
Taking k = 1:
p(x) = x² - x + 1.
[ROUGH_WORK]
D = (-1)² - 4(1)(1) = 1 - 4 = -3 < 0.
Boxed Answer: [ Required quadratic polynomial is x² - x + 1 ].
concept_questions: Can you form a valid quadratic polynomial even when its discriminant is negative?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q2 (v): Find a quadratic polynomial with sum = -1/4, product = 1/4.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: S = -1/4, P = 1/4.
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - Sx + P ] = k [ x² - (-1/4)x + 1/4 ] = k [ x² + x/4 + 1/4 ]
Choose k = 4:
p(x) = 4(x² + x/4 + 1/4) = 4x² + x + 1.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Sum = -b/a = -1/4
Product = c/a = 1/4
Boxed Answer: [ Required quadratic polynomial is 4x² + x + 1 ].
concept_questions: Notice the middle term is positive because the given sum was negative: why is that?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 2.2 Q2 (vi): Find a quadratic polynomial with sum = 4, product = 1.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: S = 4, P = 1.
Formula: p(x) = k [ x² - Sx + P ] = k [ x² - 4x + 1 ]
Taking k = 1:
p(x) = x² - 4x + 1.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Zeroes: x = (4 ± √(16 - 4))/2 = (4 ± √12)/2 = 2 ± √3
Sum = (2 + √3) + (2 - √3) = 4
Product = (2 + √3)(2 - √3) = 4 - 3 = 1
Boxed Answer: [ Required quadratic polynomial is x² - 4x + 1 ].
concept_questions: Notice that the roots 2 + √3 and 2 - √3 are conjugate surds: when do surd roots occur in pairs?

worked_examples.problem: Board Exam HOTS Question: If α and β are the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial p(x) = 2x² - 5x + 7, find the value of: (i) 1/α + 1/β, and (ii) α² + β².
worked_examples.solution:
Given: p(x) = 2x² - 5x + 7
Here a = 2, b = -5, c = 7.
Sum of zeroes: α + β = -b/a = -(-5)/2 = 5/2
Product of zeroes: α · β = c/a = 7/2

Part (i): Evaluate 1/α + 1/β
Taking LCM: 1/α + 1/β = (β + α) / (αβ) = (α + β) / (αβ)
Substitution:
1/α + 1/β = (5/2) / (7/2) = (5/2) × (2/7) = 5/7.

Part (ii): Evaluate α² + β²
Use algebraic identity: (α + β)² = α² + 2αβ + β²
⇒ α² + β² = (α + β)² - 2αβ
Substitution:
α² + β² = (5/2)² - 2(7/2) = 25/4 - 14/2 = 25/4 - 28/4 = -3/4.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Why is α² + β² negative? Because D = (-5)² - 4(2)(7) = 25 - 56 = -31 < 0.
The roots are complex numbers, where the sum of squares can indeed be negative!
Boxed Answer: [ (i) 1/α + 1/β = 5/7, (ii) α² + β² = -3/4 ].
concept_questions: Why did we not attempt to find the individual values of α and β directly?
How can you evaluate α³ + β³ using only the sum and product of zeroes?

          <text x="24" y="48" fill="#64748B" font-size="11" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif">Fundamental algebraic bridges connecting polynomial roots to its standard coefficients</text>
        </g>
        
  
    <g transform="translate(60, 70)">
      <rect width="460" height="230" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#CBD5E1" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/>
      <text x="24" y="32" fill="#0F172A" font-size="14" font-weight="700">Quadratic Polynomial: p(x) = ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0)</text>
      
      <!-- Sum of zeroes -->
      <rect x="24" y="50" width="412" height="42" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#93C5FD" rx="6"/>
      <text x="36" y="76" fill="#1E40AF" font-size="13" font-weight="700">Sum of Zeroes: α + β = -b / a = -(Coefficient of x) / (Coefficient of x²)</text>
      
      <!-- Product of zeroes -->
      <rect x="24" y="102" width="412" height="42" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#86EFAC" rx="6"/>
      <text x="36" y="128" fill="#166534" font-size="13" font-weight="700">Product of Zeroes: α · β = c / a = (Constant term) / (Coefficient of x²)</text>
      
      <!-- Polynomial Formation -->
      <rect x="24" y="154" width="412" height="52" fill="#FFFBEB" stroke="#FDE68A" rx="6"/>
      <text x="36" y="174" fill="#92400E" font-size="11" font-weight="700">Polynomial Formation Formula:</text>
      <text x="36" y="194" fill="#B45309" font-size="13" font-weight="700">p(x) = k [ x² - (α + β)x + (α · β) ]  where k is any non-zero real constant</text>
    </g>
    
</svg>
